title: Speech much slower than slide plan
title_ko: 슬라이드 진행보다 발화가 지나치게 느린 발표
description: The presenter lingers on the opening slide with slow speech and an anecdote. One pace prompt brings the talk back on track.

events.transcript_chunk: So... reading papers. We all, uh, skim dozens of papers every week.
And when a passage is dense... we end up re-reading it, again and again.

ground_truth.note: Slow, but still within the planned time for slide 1.

events.transcript_chunk: Let me tell you about a time when I, um, spent a whole afternoon on one paper...

ground_truth.note: 40 s over the slide plan with slow speech and a digression.

events.transcript_chunk: Right, so the problem: a static PDF cannot react when you struggle.
Highlighting tools exist, but they are manual.
GazeFlow uses a webcam to spot regressions while you read.

ground_truth.note: Still about a minute behind plan, but the pace is back to normal and the remaining time is sufficient.

events.transcript_chunk: Dense terms open a glossary pop-up, and everything stays local.
We tested 24 participants, within-subjects, against a baseline reader without adaptation.
Comprehension rose 18 percent over that baseline.
The limitation is low light: the webcam accuracy drops.
In short, attention-aware reading is feasible today.
